task.description: Gate the implemented fix against idiom, supervision integrity, scope creep, and decision-record consistency, per .claude/agents/reviewer.md's 4-question checklist.
acceptance_criteria: Idiom check: does the fix match the module's own established pattern-match convention
Supervision check: does this pure module touch any supervision-tree concern
Scope creep check: does the fix stay within the 3 named functions or add unrequested abstraction
Decision-record consistency: does the fix contradict req044-transition-kernel.md's design

result.summary: Read `git diff lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex` directly (3 one-line changes) plus the full file and req044-transition-kernel.md design doc. (1) Idiomatic vs. crutch: not applicable in the gen_statem/GenServer sense -- this module has no process, no state machine, it's a pure function module (design doc §8's purity contract). The fix itself IS the idiomatic choice among the alternatives: dispatch_node/4's own existing 5 clauses already use `%Node{node_type: :X} = node`-shaped pattern matches to narrow a parameter's type for the compiler; this fix applies the identical convention to instance_state/token in the 3 functions one call-level down, rather than introducing a different mechanism (e.g. a runtime `is_struct/2` guard clause, or an Access-behaviour-based workaround) that would be inconsistent with the file's own established style. (2) Supervision: not applicable -- transition.ex has zero relationship to Letflow.InstanceSupervisor or any supervised process; this fix touches nothing in that tree. (3) Scope creep: none -- diff touches exactly 3 lines in 3 already-existing private function signatures; no new function, no new module, no new abstraction, no behaviour/macro added. Explicitly checked that dispatch_node/4 itself (the function ISS-0046's own original filed hypothesis suspected needed editing) was NOT touched -- confirmed via `git diff --stat`, matching the design's own §3 negative-scope statement. (4) Decision-record consistency: fix does not contradict req044-transition-kernel.md -- that design's §6 dispatch table and §6.1-§6.3 per-case behavior are unaffected; no field type, no error tuple shape, no dispatch order changed. Type-safety-gap check (checklist item 3, non-blocking): none found -- this fix is itself closing a type-safety gap (the compiler's own type checker), not introducing a new representable-invalid-state class. No anti-patterns.md entry applies to this change (checked current entries; none concern struct-update type inference).
